translation: The most important event in the winter of 1993 for me was my father's return, just a week before my mom remarried.
One afternoon in December, he came to find me at school.
I sprinted towards the front gate and from a distance, through the iron railings, I saw him outside smoking.
He wore a black long-sleeved coat with an upright collar that hid half of his face.
For some unknown reason, without even clearly seeing his face, I felt as if he was not doing well.
My heart saddened and tears welled up in my eyes.
I never thought my mother would consider remarrying.
Perhaps subconsciously, I felt she should continue to suffer because of my father's departure, just like me.
Moreover, I felt that she lacked the ability to find happiness again.
Maybe that was indeed the case, but happiness can still find her.
After all, as a beautiful woman, she didn't have to work hard; she didn't have to do anything but stand in place.
I still remember that winter was particularly long that year, and the flowering apricot did not bloom until halfway through April.
My parents' divorce caused you to become very depressed.
We haven't had any new games for a long time, and when evening comes, we just sit aimlessly on the roof of the Tower of Death.
A few more arms were added among the body parts scattered in the yard.
We used hooks to pull them together, arranging them into a thousand-armed Bodhisattva.
Actually, my father didn't know the first thing about business.
He just went to rely on a cousin who wasn't even close.
My grandmother had a sister who moved to Beijing in her early years and later married and had children there.
This older cousin was her eldest son, who has always been considered an alien within the entire family.
You just said that everyone has a time when their destiny takes hold, as if life suddenly reins them in.
For me, it was when I was eight years old.
That autumn, my father left Jinan and made his way to Beijing on his own.
After that, I no longer had a home.
I didn't plan on keeping the appointment.
Whatever the reason, I don't think there was any need for us to see each other again.
I sat on the sofa smoking one cigarette after another, as it grew darker and darker outside.
Suddenly, there was a knock at the door.
The water delivery boy stood in front of the doorway with his water buckets, saying that he needed to make a delivery to a household in the western suburbs.
He wore a dirty grey wool cap and had a vacant look on his face.
Our conversation was incredibly difficult.
Each time we fell into silence, I felt my heart being squeezed and I just wanted to end the encounter quickly.
You seemed to sense this but still tried to find new topics.
The tea grew cold, and the fog in the room dissipated as you finally stood up to leave.
Just as I shut the door with a sigh of relief, the doorbell rang again.
There you were at my doorstep, inviting me over to Xiao Bai Tower later in the evening.
I barely had time to refuse before you had already disappeared from sight.
I went to the kitchen and turned off the stove.
Half a pot of water had evaporated, filling the room with a white mist.
You sat down uncomfortably, watching me pour tea.
"Are you still living with your grandmother and aunt?" you asked.
I told you that my grandmother has passed away, and I am now living with my aunt.
"She never got married" you asked .
"Yes.
The white breath you exhaled, the curling hair lifted by the wind, and your knees slightly trembling beneath the hem of your coat.
.. all of these made me believe in your real presence before my eyes.
It's not a continuation of that previous dream.
We haven't seen each other for eighteen years, so it's not surprising I hardly recognized you.
You didn't have any makeup on: your pale face was slightly swollen, yet you still lived up to everyone's expectations and became a beautiful woman.
However, there was a hint of gloom in your small peach-shaped face; it carried an air of having spent too long in the big city.
You asked me if you look different from what I imagined.
I just smiled noncommittally.
To be honest, I've never imagined what you would look like when grown up.
As far as I'm concerned, everything related to you has been put into a document bag and sealed with wax—I don't expect us to meet again which might sound harsh but that's how it is.
I opened my eyes.
You were standing in the doorway.
I had no idea how long you'd been there, maybe you even saw me laughing in my sleep, the melancholy of waking up, and my most vulnerable moments.
"Cheng Gong," you said quietly, your voice hoarse as if you hadn't spoken aloud for a long time.
It's going to snow soon; it's terribly overcast and pitch black inside the house.
The water on the stove was boiling, bubbling away noisily.
I studied your face carefully, certain that I did not recognize who you were.
However under the dim light it suddenly felt like this stranger standing in front of me had some deep connection with my life a feeling that sent chills down my spine.
Wracking my memory as images turned over rapidly in mind and then.
you introduced yourself as Li Jiaqi.
